items.title: Repair both slow-board CI performance failures
items.symptom: SLOW_212608 and SLOW_202111 measured491.433/493.853ms against the unchanged480ms bound on master c310005.
items.existing_work: Earlier cache/key optimizations are merged; this repeat failure is unresolved. Original desktop session ended while profiling.
acceptance: Preserve480ms bounds, search budgets and all meaningful assertions; no fixture-specific shortcuts.
Matched before/after profiling and payload/node-count/mutation checks show a genuine repair, with focused tests passing.
A real Linux CI receipt is required to claim CI is green; local timings alone are not that receipt.

implementation.note: Repaired in an isolated worktree (/tmp/wt-ciperf) at master 34ee704 and merged to local master as c66155c. The block search now caches per-body fight keys, material, death-trigger swings and hit flags per search, starts every assignment from a precomputed unblocked baseline and adds only the deltas of the attackers a choice touches, reuses its per-choice scratch, and skips the menace check when no attacker has menace; combat_detail keys protection through _protection_part, which collapses to () when no fight body can be affected by protection, and protection_signature has a plain fast path that still takes the slow path for printed unpreventable damage. SLOW_212608 103.3 -> 87.1 ms and SLOW_202111 101.9 -> 87.4 ms on this machine with identical node/combat counts (90/396 and 185/310). Differential replay of all 2,771 block searches across 29 strategic boards against c310005: 0 mismatches. Focused regressions: 501 passed; ruff clean. BLOCKER: acceptance criterion 3 needs a real Linux CI receipt and this session may not push or deploy, so CI green is unconfirmed; extrapolating the failing run's own CI/local ratio predicts ~415/~424 ms against the unchanged 480 ms bound.
